location: San Cristobal de Mangas, Ancash, Peru
provenance: Found 2003 by Rebeca Arcayo Aguado in wooden trunk in church sanctuary
description_source: Robles Mendoza 1982 (earlier board); Hyland Ware & Clark 2014 (current board)
document_purpose: Padrón: register of ritual/labor obligations (feast of Masha, Virgin of Rosary); fulfillment tracking
reliability_notes: Best-documented board. Multispectral imaging recovered faded names. Moiety-knot correlation verified 15/15. Note: Robles 1982 described a DIFFERENT board (110 names Side A, 209 holes) vs current (150 names Side A, 207 holes) — either replaced or earlier state.

document_purpose: Single variable, likely mass attendance; names in strict male/female alternation suggesting priest-compiled
reliability_notes: Poorly documented. Three layers of paper (reused 3x). Simple cords lack color complexity of Mangas. No cord-level analysis published.

location: San Pedro de Casta, Huarochiri, Lima, Peru
provenance: Village use; described by Tello 1923; Entablo ms 1921
current_location: Hidden by villagers; not accessible (per Hyland et al. 2021)
description_source: Tello & Miranda 1923 (drawing); Entablo manuscript (Bennison ed.); Hyland Bennison & Hyland 2021; Bennison 2025 preprint
document_purpose: Champeria (annual canal-cleaning) labor tribute; multiple boards for different ceremonies; separate men/women records; punishment tracking (whipping/hair-cutting for slackers)
reliability_notes: Rich contextual documentation via Entablo but NO surviving board accessible for cord-level study. Leather (not yarn) cords per Bennison 2025. Knots hypothesized = sequential task completion.

document_purpose: Catechism attendance; cords pulled tight = fulfilled, left hanging = punished (3 lashes)
reliability_notes: Eyewitness description only. No physical board studied. Confirms operational mechanism (tight/loose = fulfilled/unfulfilled).
